message.content: In Christian tradition, the emphasis is often on Jesus Christ as the central figure—he is seen as the fulfillment of prophetic expectations rather than a prophet in the same sense as those in the Hebrew Bible. However, many Christians also regard certain Old Testament figures—such as Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and others—as significant prophets whose teachings and actions shaped the faith’s foundations. Different denominations and theological perspectives may highlight various prophets or emphasize particular aspects of their roles, so there isn’t a single universally agreed-upon “most important” prophet outside of the central role attributed to Jesus himself.
